description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while auditing perl-tests/range.t's inline
`ok(1,'SKIP')` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

REPRO (scratch/p37-sse-range2.pl):

    my $y = 'X'; $y =~ s/X/join ':', 'a' .. 'e'/e;   print "[$y]\n";
    my $w = 'X'; $w =~ s/X/scalar(join ':', 1 .. 3)/e; print "[$w]\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  [a:b:c:d:e]   [1:2:3]
  PCL:          [1E0]         []
  and PCL also prints, twice: "Use of uninitialized value $. in numeric eq (==)"

"1E0" IS the flip-flop's true value, and the `$.` read is the flip-flop's
constant-operand rule -- so the operator chosen for `..` inside the s///e
replacement is the SCALAR flip-flop, not the range/list operator.

THE EXTENT IS NARROW, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A GOOD FIX (probed,
scratch/p35-range-ctx.pl + p37): ALL SEVEN ordinary list-context spellings are
correct -- `my @a = ('a'..'e')`, `join ':', 'a'..'e'`, the same with variable
operands, numeric, `my @b = ($p..$q)`, and `join ':', $1 .. $2` OUTSIDE a
s///e.  Inside the replacement, `join ':', 1, 2, 3` (a plain list) is correct
and `f()` where `sub f { join ':', 1 .. 3 }` is correct.  Only `..` written
LITERALLY in the replacement diverges.  So the replacement expression is
compiled by a path that gives its arguments scalar context, and everything
else about it works.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/range.t's inline skip at the `s///e` block
("PCL: s///e eval does not propagate list context to ..").  Its two
neighbours, `eval "-0x7fffffff..-0x7ffffffe"` in list context, are the SAME
symptom reached through string eval and are covered by
docs/not-supported.md 'Context propagation into string eval' -- but the s///e
half has NO eval in it, so that entry does not explain this one.  Both rows in
the companion t/op/range.t are inside its blessed count.

NOT #141.  #141 is the flip-flop's OWN semantics (a constant operand must
compare against `$.` per-operand).  This is the choice of flip-flop over
range in the first place.  #141's fix would make the wrong answer here a
different wrong answer.

FIX SHAPE (untried): find where the s///e replacement expression is lowered
and give it the same context an ordinary expression statement gets, so the
range-vs-flip-flop selection point sees list context for `join`'s arguments.
Acceptance = the five rows of scratch/p37-sse-range2.pl agreeing with perl.
See #1026 for a second defect in the same lowering (a `map {}` in the
replacement does not transpile at all).
subject: SILENT WRONG: inside an `s///e` REPLACEMENT, `..` is lowered as the scalar FLIP-FLOP even in list context -- `s/X/join ':', 'a'..'e'/e` substitutes the flip-flop value "1E0" instead of a:b:c:d:e (and reads $.); every other list-context spelling of `..` is correct
